text:
Tanya Miller: Quick sync note — customer B is asking for 6y audit retention, per-tenant toggle, and an exports UI for auditors. Need to scope MVP vs opt-ins for pricing and compliance.

Omar Aziz: MVP should guarantee SOC2/ISO proper evidence: legal_hold API, immutable manifests, and BYOK support. Searchable cold index can be an opt-in paid feature.

Leah Kim: Legal: any exported evidence must be complete and provably untampered. That means manifest hashes, signature, key fingerprint, and a legal_hold timeline. Sampling or lossy compaction is not acceptable for audit requests.

Victor Santos: Engineering constraints: cold storage = object WORM + manifest.json (SHA256 list) + signature. Rehydrate path: fetch objects -> verify manifest -> reindex. Throughput approx 40-60 GB/hr per restore node.

Tanya Miller: Pricing question — do we do pay-per-restore or a monthly searchable surcharge? Both?

Omar Aziz: Recommend two-tier commercial model: (1) long-term archive base fee (covers storage + BYOK plumbing), (2) searchable-cold add-on (monthly) OR ad-hoc restore charges at cost. 

Leah Kim: Legal prefers searchable-cold for heavy e-discovery customers but accepts pay-per-restore as long as SLA and chain-of-custody are documented. Also require removal of legal_hold require a recorded Legal approval event.

ArchivalBot: [system] Policy snippet detected: retention_profiles draft uploaded by Omar Aziz. Running compliance checks.

Victor Santos: Operational SLAs we can realistically commit to for MVP: subset rehydrate search <8h, targeted reindex <24h, full archive reindex <72h (depends on size). Need indexed hot window of 1-2 years to reduce restore scope.

Tanya Miller: Proposal for default profiles (RFC-ready):
```yaml
retention_profiles:
  trial:
    hot_days: 90
    metadata_years: 1
    cold_years: 0
  standard:
    hot_days: 365
    metadata_years: 1
    cold_years: 3
  enterprise_archive:
    hot_days: 365
    metadata_years: 2
    cold_years: 6
    byok_support: true
    legal_hold_support: true
    searchable_cold: optional
```

Leah Kim: Ensure legal_hold overrides TTL and creates an immutable audit event with actor, timestamp, justification, and case_id. Exports of the event history must include a signed snapshot hash.

Omar Aziz: BYOK nuance: for hosted customers allow KMS key-id + wrapped envelope keys stored in escrow for recovery; for private deployments support HSM direct. For >5y retention, Legal wants BYOK strongly recommended.

Victor Santos: Monitoring: track restore queue depth, average restore cost/GB, error rate, and spike alerts. Ops runbook: escrow key prove, manifest fail modes, and fallback to customer-provided proofs.

Tanya Miller: Roadmap ask: ship MVP (legal_hold API + BYOK plumbing + cold WORM + manifest signing + restore runbook) in Q3; make searchable-cold pilot in Q4. Any blockers?

Leah Kim: Blocker: finalize legal approval flow for removal and export notarization. Also need legal to sign off on BYOK edge cases.

Omar Aziz: Tech blocker: finalize manifest signing SDK and escrow logging format. I'll own a small prototype.

Victor Santos: I'll prototype restore pipeline and rough perf numbers for the RFC.

ArchivalBot: [system] RFC created: /docs/retention/rfc-enterprise-archive-mvp.md

Tanya Miller: Thanks — I'll put this on the board as "Enterprise archive MVP (BYOK + legal_hold + WORM manifests)" and assign owners: Omar (BYOK + manifest), Victor (restore), Leah (legal runbook). Decision required at next roadmap sync.
